newsitem.title: USA: Ill Attorney General seeks to shut Clark refinery.
newsitem.headline: Ill Attorney General seeks to shut Clark refinery.

text.p: Illinois Attorney General Jim Ryan said Monday he plans to seek a court order to temporarily shut down a Clark Refining & Marketing Inc refinery in Illinois until it is proven safe.

The 80,000 barrel-a-day Blue Island refinery had an explosion and fire in a propane scrubber Saturday, which Ryan said in a news release was the latest in a series of safety related incidents at the refinery in recent years.
Clark said there were no injuries from the explosion and fire Saturday.
But on March 13, 1995, two workers were killed and three others injured in an explosion at the refinery's Isomax unit.

In May of that year, fifteen pounds of hydrofluroic acid leaked from an alkylation unit at the plant, Ryan said, adding that 25 students at a high school one-quarter mile away complained of lightheadedness and related symptoms.
Ryan also cited several incidents of emmission discharges in 1995 and 1994.
Clark officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
